s: DNS, TCP/IP, how the web actually works
d: Before writing backend code, understand how the internet works. Every request travels through DNS resolution, TCP connections, and IP routing. Knowing this helps you debug network issues, optimize performance, and understand why things like CDNs and load balancers exist.
c: How a URL becomes a webpage
Domain registrars & DNS records (A, CNAME, MX)

p: The Internet is a global network of interconnected networks. It relies on standard protocols like TCP/IP to route packets of data from a source IP address to a destination IP address across routers and switches.
2. Browser queries DNS for the IP address.
3. Browser opens a TCP connection to the IP.
5. Server processes and sends HTTP response.

# Traceroute shows the path packets take across the internet
traceroute google.com
1  192.168.1.1 (Router)
2  10.0.0.1 (ISP)
3  ... (Backbone)

[User/Browser] ---> (ISP) ---> [Internet Backbone] ---> [Server]
   198.51.100.1                                    203.0.113.5
Data is broken into "packets". Each packet finds its own route.
